evidence: Dimension level: task/tests/scoring.toml is byte-identical (cmp) to the frozen template scoring.toml: [gates] render=0.0 constraints=0.0; [weights] functional=0.6 polish=0.2 visual=0.2; [floors] functional=0.05. Functional alone (0.6) outweighs polish+visual combined (0.4). task/tests/tools/score.py is identical to the template (diff empty): reward = weighted mean only when gates pass and functional > 0.05, else 0. No judge.toml [judge] block carries weight/model/temperature/reasoning_effort (parsed keys: judge, mode, timeout, isolated, prompt_template, mcp_servers). Criterion level (parsed with tomllib): functional 43 binary criteria, total weight 58.5, range 0.5-2.5 (max share 4.27%, min 0.85%); polish 5 binary, total 12 (3, 3, 2, 1.5, 2.5); visual 5 likert points=5, each 1.2 (uniform 20%), each with five described anchors; gates 1 binary each, weight 1.0, all_pass. Weight tracks what each criterion proves and mirrors the brief's stated emphasis ('the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled'): heaviest functional rows are hro_stale_refused 2.5 (stale move refused naming the colleague), hro_live_board 2.5 (15 s live board), hro_candidate_private 2.5 (no leakage of notes/reasons/other candidates), hro_bulk_all_or_none 2, hro_undo_restores 2, hro_undo_conflict 2, hro_refused_put_back 2, hro_thread_earlier 2, hro_unread_counts 2, hro_unread_scrolled_up 2, hro_drafts 2; lightest are setup-like or narrow edge rows that prove little beyond their siblings: hro_job_open 0.5, hro_add_candidate 0.5 (prerequisites that most other rows depend on), hro_reject_hired 0.5, hro_undo_full 0.5, hro_activity_refusals 0.5, hro_candidate_linked 0.5. Polish rows are not cosmetic: every one requires working live/messaging/session behaviour (live update preserving open card, typed note, focus and scroll; live thread preserving draft; earlier-load place; failed-send recovery; session-expiry draft resume), so a non-live app earns ~0 polish, which keeps non-functional mass from rewarding a dead app. Max non-functional contribution sanity check: polish+visual can contribute at most 0.4; per the visual prompt (lines 12, 16) a blank/static shell gets Likert 1 = normalized 0, and the functional floor 0.05 (about 3 weight units of 58.5) blocks a near-dead app. Weak-app attempt: a pretty CRUD-only app (job_open, add_candidate, add_email_rules, move_one_stage, arrive_bottom, reorder, restart = 7.5/58.5 = 0.128 functional), no live/messaging, polish 0, visual 1.0 -> 0.6*0.128 + 0.2*1.0 = 0.277; a functionally strong but plain app (functional 0.84 missing all live/unread rows, polish 0.5, visual 0.4) -> 0.504+0.1+0.08 = 0.684; full-functional ugly app (functional 1, polish 1, visual 0) -> 0.8. Ordering follows functionality. Inversions are possible only when functional differences are under ~0.33 against a full visual swing, which is the template-mandated 0.6/0.2/0.2 policy the skill says to apply and must not be altered. Conforming-alternative attempt: weights alone cannot make a conforming app fail; no criterion carries disproportionate mass (max 4.3% of functional, 2.6% of reward), so a single misjudged row cannot swing a conforming app materially. Minor observation (not a defect): hro_activity (a whole required staff view, strict conjunctive bar) is weight 1 plus hro_activity_refusals 0.5 = 2.6% of functional; arguably light for a required view but defensible because it is one observable family. Out of scope for this row but noted: raw-evidence-index.json states full configured grading, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent; RewardKit likert normalization and actual judge scoring were not observed. This row's claim is structural weight arithmetic, which was fully measured from the frozen files; empirical reward ordering belongs to row 42 and the runtime records.
